claims.explanation: Rivaroxaban is a direct factor Xa (F10) inhibitor, so cancer cells that depend on a tissue factor–FXa–PAR autocrine loop for proliferation/survival are expected to be selectively killed. High expression of F10, F3, F7, F2R, and F2RL1 would increase this dependency, while high efflux transporters (ABCB1/ABCG2) would reduce intracellular drug and protect. Enriched damaging mutations in ARID1A, KRAS, and KMT2D in the sensitive lines may further upregulate the coagulation axis.
